tagline: Four miles of old turnpike to the Housatonic arches.
intro: From Old Sharon Road, Route 4 runs about four miles east on the line of the old Sharon and Cornwall Turnpike and comes to US 7 at Cornwall Bridge, where the two roads cross the Housatonic together.

A few miles south of Cornwall Bridge lay Dudleytown, a farm settlement named for the Dudley family, who came there from the 1740s. It emptied out after the Midwest opened in the mid-19th century and the local iron trade wound down, and only cellar holes are left. Ghost stories brought vandals in the 1980s, and the owners have closed it to the public.

moments.title: Cornwall Bridge
moments.text: After the new bridge went up in 1930 the village center slowly moved uphill from the river to Route 7 and Route 4, and the old covered bridge went out in the 1936 flood.

moments.title: Bridge No. 560
moments.text: Six open-spandrel concrete arches, the largest such bridge in the state, carry the road over the Housatonic and the railroad, with the old station, unserved since 1972, below.
